title: Strict mode, and the sharp edges it turns off

videos.script:
Some mistakes in JavaScript make no sound. {{silent}} Assign to a variable you never declared, and a global appears. Change a frozen object, and the change is ignored. Nothing is printed, nothing stops, and the program carries on with a value that is wrong.

{{why}} That was a choice made in the first years of the language, so that pages written carelessly would still mostly work. It was the wrong choice for programs anybody has to maintain, and in 2009 the language added a way to turn it off: strict mode.

{{loud}} In strict mode, the silent mistakes throw. A typo in a variable name becomes a ReferenceError at the line with the typo. An assignment that cannot happen becomes a TypeError. And a few old features that made code hard to reason about are not allowed at all.

{{auto}} The good news is that you rarely have to ask for it. Modules and classes are strict automatically, so most code written today already runs that way. {{where}} The lesson ends with where sloppy mode still survives, because that is where you will meet these bugs.
